text.tspan: Future directions

text.style: font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;font-stretch:normal;font-size:46.6667px;font-family:'Liberation Serif', 'Times New Roman', serif;-inkscape-font-specification:'Liberation Serif, Times New Roman, serif';white-space:pre;shape-inside:url(#rect755);display:inline;fill:#000000
text.tspan: GPCRs, also known as G protein-coupled receptors, are by far the most
diverse and broadly distributed family of membrane-resident receptors.
These proteins are responsible for cellular signaling in many diverse

tspan.tspan: pathways that are involved in important cellular decisions. As of recent,

text.tspan: GPCR-targeting drugs are estimated to represent 30-50% of all prescribed
drugs.
Many GPCRs form dimers that have two transmembrane domains (one per
protein), and there are indications that this dimeric interaction is functionally
meaningful.

font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;font-stretch:normal;font-size:46.6667px;font-family:'Liberation Serif', 'Times New Roman', serif;-inkscape-font-specification:'Liberation Serif, Times New Roman, serif';white-space:pre;shape-inside:url(#rect12288);display:inline;fill:#000000
text.tspan: Identifying and understanding
multi-domain GPCRs could:
Deepen our understanding of
GPCR oligomerization.
Support evolutionary theories
on protein duplication, emergence,
and divergence.
Shed light on membrane
proteins and their complex
formations.

text.style: font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;font-stretch:normal;font-size:46.6667px;font-family:'Liberation Serif', 'Times New Roman', serif;-inkscape-font-specification:'Liberation Serif, Times New Roman, serif';white-space:pre;shape-inside:url(#rect12296);shape-padding:0.956383;display:inline;fill:#000000
text.tspan: So far, we have identified 57 representative multi-domain GPCR
proteins :
They contain the functional motifs that are conserved in single-
GPCRs that allow coupling to G-proteins.

tspan.tspan: Distributed in chordates, narrower than known single GPCRs.

text.tspan: Many olfactory receptors and few chemokine receptors identified.

tspan.tspan: Olfactory receptors are over-represented in land-dwelling animals:
might be a consequence of the olfactory expansion, with the need to

text.tspan: recognize many volatile odorants.
Chemokine receptors seem to be specific to aquatic animals, which
should be investigated in future projects.
There seems to be putative olfactory multi-GPCRs in some
primates.

text.tspan: 1) Class C (e.g. glutamate receptors) form obligate dimers in
physiological conditions: expanding the search procedure to possibly
find multi-GPCRs with Class C homology.
2) Finding other multi-GPCRs from all classes that are known to
oligomerize
3) Exhaustive phylogenetic analysis to fill in the "gaps"
4) Untangling their evolutionary advantage and contribution
